The summer in between my Freshman Sophomore year of college (2024), I signed up to go on the 10 day sea turtle field course in Ostional, Costa Rica. Here, I gained valuable experience in field work, data collection and learned a lot about local conservation management strategies around the Olive Ridley Sea Turtle species. Data collection consisted of night patrols from 8pm-12am or 12am-4am where we counted turtle abundance, measured the turtle, clutch size, counted the number of eggs laid and the time it took to do so. 

![](images/work.jpg)

During my time in Ostional, I got to witness an arribada (mass nesting event), which took place across 3 days. Here we saw thousands on female turtles come up the beach to nest. 

![](images/arribada.jpg)

I will forever cherish this experience and it is what has encouraged me to get involved in species conservation and take the ENVS 193ST: Sea Turtle Conservation and Management course at UCSB.
